_comment: TOTOY scenario data. Contains Levels 1-4 definitions to show curriculum scope, but scenarios are trimmed to just Level 1 for the pitch demo.

ambient.speaker: Kid at Unit 4
ambient.speech_bubble: Uy Totoy! Panalo ka daw! 1 millionth visitor ka oh!
ambient.subtitle: Hey Totoy! It says you won! You're the 1 millionth visitor!

suriin.summary: Why is a random website giving away a phone and internet credits?

clues.label: Oldest Trick
clues.note: This is a classic internet scam template. Real websites do not track random visitors to give out expensive prizes.

clues.label: Data Harvesting
clues.note: They don't want to give you a prize; they want your personal information to send you spam or sell it to other scammers.

choices.text: Type in your name and number to claim the prize

outcome.kuya_tip: That's a data harvesting scam! They just want to collect your full name, email, and phone number. The '1,000,000th visitor' is one of the oldest tricks on the internet.

choices.text: Close the window and ignore the fake prize

outcome.kuya_tip: Nice save! If a random pop-up asks for your personal information in exchange for a 'free prize', you are the product. [b]Never give your data to unverified sites.[/b]

ambient.speaker: Kid at next PC
ambient.speech_bubble: Totoy, i-download mo na 'yan! Baka masira 'yang PC, singilin ka pa ni Kuya!
ambient.subtitle: Totoy, you better download that! If you break the PC, Kuya will make you pay for it!

suriin.summary: How can a random website know what is inside this computer?

clues.label: Impossible Tech
clues.note: A web page cannot scan your local hard drive. The virus alert is just a scare tactic.

clues.label: File Type
clues.note: Clicking 'Install FREE' downloads an executable program. If you run it, it takes control of the PC.

choices.text: Click 'Install FREE' to clean the viruses

outcome.kuya_tip: That's scareware! They scare you with fake virus alerts so you willingly install their malware. The truth: [b]no website can scan your computer[/b].

choices.text: Close the entire window via the top title bar

outcome.kuya_tip: Correct! You closed it from the outer title bar, not the fake ad buttons. Remember: on a public PisoNet PC, [b]never install random software[/b].
